The Ship of Theseus: if every plank of a ship is replaced over the years, is it still the same ship? Which parts of you have been replaced and are still you?
Rawls' veil of ignorance: design a fair world without knowing who you'll be in it. What changes about how you'd build it?
Hilbert's Hotel: a hotel with infinitely many rooms is full, yet it can still fit one more guest by shifting everyone over a room. What in your life seems full but could shift to make room?
Nozick's experience machine: you could plug into a machine that gives you any experiences you choose, but it isn't real. Would you go in? What does your answer say about what you value?
Buridan's donkey: a donkey placed exactly between two identical piles of hay starves because it can't choose. When is picking either option better than not picking?
Zeno's arrow: at any single instant an arrow in flight is motionless, so how does it move? What progress of yours is invisible one moment at a time?
The thousand-year-old tree: you plant a tree you will never sit under. What would you plant, and for whom?
